country: Multinational (USA internal cohort; China, Germany, Spain)
models_evaluated: AI-based %RVT scoring algorithm (digital pathology, H&E slides)

links.outcome: AI concordance with manual %RVT across sites and scanners
links.effect: Concordance at least moderate across all cohorts; pooled MPR accuracy 91% (95% CI 85-95), sensitivity 90%, specificity 93%, AUC ≥0.95 in all cohorts.
links.quote: Concordance between AI-based and manual assessment was at least moderate across all cohorts.

links.outcome: AI performance on external multicenter validation cohorts against consensus reference standard
links.effect: Three external cohorts (China, Germany, Spain; 97 patients) showed pooled MPR accuracy of 91% (85-95) and AUC ≥0.95 in all cohorts.
links.quote: For major pathologic response (MPR) classification, the AI algorithm achieved a pooled accuracy of 91% (95% CI, 85-95), sensitivity of 90% (82-95), specificity of 93% (81-99), and an area under the curve ≥0.95 in all cohorts.

unlisted_practices: Weighted consensus of multiple pathologists as reference standard

screen.reason: The study conducts an international multicenter retrospective validation and error analysis of an AI model for pathologic response scoring on digital pathology slides, but does not test a specific organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
